\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-104},
  title = {The containers log to the VM's journal, so their logs survive a deploy},
  date = {2026-11-07},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Deployment, Monitoring},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (options, measurements, implementation)},
  decision = {Every container logs through Docker's \texttt{journald} driver (the \texttt{x-\allowbreak{}logging} anchor of \texttt{deploy/\allowbreak{}compose.\allowbreak{}yaml}); journald's own limit bounds the size, \texttt{journalctl CONTAINER\_\allowbreak{}NAME=\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}} reads the logs of replaced containers, and \texttt{docker logs} still reads the running one.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \texttt{json-\allowbreak{}file} (before) or \texttt{local}: the log of a recreated container is gone (measured).
\item A log volume per service: survives, but needs changes to nginx, the API, and the monitor, a rotation sidecar, and \texttt{docker logs} no longer shows them.
\item \texttt{deploy.\allowbreak{}sh} saving \texttt{docker logs} before \texttt{up}: covers deploys only, and the script is installed by hand.
\item Loki and Alloy: two more services and memory, and Alloy needs the Docker socket, against NFR-09.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} One line in a file that travels with each release keeps the logs of every recreate, as a throwaway stack showed.
The default cap, 2 GB of the VM's 20 GB, fits NFR-04.},
  ai = {Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI measured which options keep the log across a recreate and recommended journald.
Its burst test kept 19,998 of 30,000 lines, probably journald's rate limit, unverified, and far above NFR-03's 20 requests/s.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.
Question (translated from German, paraphrased): ``\#313: how should the containers' logs (nginx, the API, the drift job) survive a deploy? Today every recreate loses them (json-file driver, measured).''
Orchestrator briefing (core, paraphrased): ``Do \#312, and lay out \#313's options (journald driver, local driver, a log volume per service, Loki): for each, measure whether logs survive a recreate, where the size cap is set, how an operator reads them, and what changes on the VM; end with DECISION NEEDED.''
Lukas answered: ``journald driver: one line in the x-logging anchor of compose.yaml; logs survive every recreate (measured), readable with journalctl CONTAINER\_NAME=..., docker logs keeps working for the running container. journald caps the size (default 10\,\% of the disk, at most 4 GB); on the VM the deploy user joins systemd-journal. In the burst test only 19,998 of 30,000 lines arrived (probably the rate limit, unverified); far below at 20 req/s.'' (translated from German)},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/issues/313}{Issue \#313}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/monitoring.md\#logs}{Logs}, EDN-94.},
